description: Ask the user in the spreadsheet grid and wait for their answer — use it when the work cannot proceed without a decision that is genuinely theirs. One question: pass `message` (and `options`, `range`). Several related decisions: pass `questions` instead — they are shown as steps of ONE dialog, each at its own cells, and answered together. Returns the chosen option id(s), or cancel (with any answers given before it). A question with options also lets the user answer in their own words ("Other"); that answer comes back as text instead of an id. ONE prompt at a time per session: while one is waiting on the user another is refused — wait for the answer or cancel that task. Pass `range` when a question is ABOUT specific cells and it is shown at them, which is most of the time; without one it is a centred dialog. To show cells WITHOUT asking anything — a findings list, a running narration — use `highlight` instead; it expects no response. Requires a session with a UI view (a workbook open in the client). On clients with task support the call returns immediately and you poll the task; on clients without it, the call blocks until the user responds. FALLBACK: if it errors because no UI session is available, ask the user the question directly in chat and proceed on their reply.

message.description: The question to show the user. Omit when passing `questions`.

options.description: Buttons to offer, e.g. [{"id":"yes","label":"Yes, update it"},{"id":"no","label":"Leave it"}]. `id` is what comes back to you; `label` is what the user reads. Omit for an acknowledge prompt (message and close only).

description.description: A second, quieter line under the label: what choosing it does.

questions.description: Several questions as steps of one dialog (up to 6), in the order asked. Use instead of `message`/`options`/`range`, for decisions that belong together.

header.description: A short name for this question's tab, e.g. "Fee format" — give one for every question; without it the tabs read "Question 1", "Question 2". A long one is shortened with an ellipsis, never refused.

id.description: What this answer comes back under. Unique within the prompt.

options.description: Buttons for this question. Omit for an acknowledge step.

description.description: A second, quieter line under the label: what choosing it does.

range.description: The range this question is about; the step is shown there.

The single sheet-qualified range the question is about, e.g. "Sheet1!B47" — the prompt appears at those cells. Omit only when the question is not about a place; it is then centred rather than anchored somewhere arbitrary.

session_id.description: Target session id, from `info` or `list_sessions`. Required.

name: prompt
